# Introduction

The ["multinomialTS Vienette"](multinomialTS-vignette.html) takes you through the fitting process, and bootstrapping, of _multinomialTS_. This vignette will show you how to fit the model at multiple binning resolutions using Sunfish Pond as an example dataset.

The data include a ~13,800-year long fossil pollen record, and a lake level reconstruction used as a proxy for hydroclimatic variability and plant water availability.


This vignette will take us through:

- Testing multiple prediction resolutions



# Data processing {#sec-data}

Before fitting a `multinomialTS` model, the raw data need to be shaped into two matrices:

- **$Y$**: a site-by-species (time-by-taxon) matrix of counts for the focal taxa, with a reference taxon in the first column.
- **$X$**: a matrix of environmental covariates, aligned to the same temporal resolution as $Y$.

Because the lake level reconstructio is built from short cores, and the pollen is from a separate lake core, they do not share a chronology. We won't be tackling any issues of alligning chronologies here! For the sake of this demonstration, we will be binning the data so that observations fall within the nearest time bin.

```{r}
#| label: libraries
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(scales)
library(multinomialTS)
library(patchwork)

# Load up the data
data(sunfish_pollen_wide)
data(sunfish_ll)
```

First let's see what the data look like:

```{r}

sunfish_pollen_long <- sunfish_pollen_wide |>
  rename(P.strobus = "P.strobu") |>
  pivot_longer(-age) |>
  mutate(name = factor(name, levels = c(
    "other", "P.strobus", "Tsuga", "Fagus", "Quercus", "Betula"))) |>
  arrange(age)

pol_plot <- ggplot(sunfish_pollen_long, aes(x = age, y = value)) +
    geom_area(colour = "grey90") +
    geom_segment(data = sunfish_pollen_long,
      aes(x = age, xend = age,
      y = 0, yend = value), colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.6) +
    scale_x_reverse(breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 6)) +
    coord_flip() +
    labs(y = "Pollen counts", x = "Time (ybp)") +
    facet_wrap(~name,
               nrow = 1) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      text = element_text(size = 10)
    )

ll_plot <- sunfish_ll |>
  mutate(panel = "Lake elevation") |>  # fake facet variable
  ggplot(aes(x = age, y = lake_lvl,
             ymin = LowerBound, ymax = UpperBound)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_ribbon(alpha = 0.3) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_x_reverse() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "cm relative to modern") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45),
    text = element_text(size = 10),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 9),
    axis.text.y = element_blank()
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~panel)
  
pol_plot + ll_plot + plot_layout(widths = c(0.85, 0.15))

```


# Prediction resoltion sensitivity

Now we are going to fit the data using multiple bin widths:

```{r}
#| label: sensitivity
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# Create some bins
bin_width <- seq(50, 150, 25)

bin_sensitivity_data <- lapply(bin_width, \(bw) {

  sunfish_bins <-
    cut(
      sunfish_pollen_wide$age,
      breaks = seq(
        from = min(sunfish_pollen_wide$age),
        to = max(sunfish_pollen_wide$age + bw),
        by = bw
      ), include.lowest = T, labels = F)

  sunfish_spp_binned <- bind_cols(bins = sunfish_bins, sunfish_pollen_wide) |>
    group_by(bins) |> # Group the data by the bins so that we calculate per time bin
    summarise(across(c("other", "P.strobu", "Tsuga", "Fagus", "Quercus", "Betula"), \(x) sum(x ,na.rm = TRUE)),
              age = mean(age, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
    arrange(desc(age))

  ll_bins <-
    cut(
      sunfish_ll$age,
      breaks = seq(
        from = min(sunfish_pollen_wide$age),
        to = max(sunfish_pollen_wide$age + bw),
        by = bw
      ), include.lowest = T, labels = F)

  ll_mean <- cbind(bins = ll_bins, sunfish_ll) |>
    drop_na(bins) |>
    select(bins, lake_lvl) |>
    group_by(bins) |>
    summarise(mean_ll = mean(lake_lvl)) |>
    arrange(desc(bins))

  # join up the data by bin
  sunfish_all <- sunfish_spp_binned |>
    full_join(ll_mean) |>
    arrange(desc(bins))

  # Final time window does not have a lake-level observation
  which(is.na(sunfish_all$mean_ll))

  # using simple linear interpolation to fill final bin
  sunfish_all_interp <- sunfish_all |>
    mutate(across(c(mean_ll), forecast::na.interp))

  Y <- sunfish_all_interp |>
    select(other, P.strobu, Tsuga, Fagus, Quercus, Betula) |>
    as.matrix()

  # set up X
  X <- sunfish_all_interp |>
    select(mean_ll) |>
    as.matrix() |>
    scale() # necessary when using multiple X variabes

  return(list(Y = Y,
              X = X))

})

names(bin_sensitivity_data) <- paste0("bw_", bin_width)
```
